description: Exactly what the webview calls, and nothing preemptive (docs/SECURITY.md §4); lib.rs pins the set with a test. core:default stood here until 1.4.0: it granted some sixty core commands nothing used and not the one the legal gate's Decline needs, so Decline did nothing in the installed app. core:event:allow-listen/unlisten carry plan-, scan-, health- and audit-progress; core:window:allow-close is Decline. dialog:allow-open is Code Health's project-folder picker and Import requirements; dialog:allow-save is Save report and Export. BOTH ONLY ASK FOR A PATH — no fs permission is granted, so the webview cannot read or write a single file. Save report hands its path to a Rust command that writes the two files, because a general fs:allow-write-text-file would be a write-anywhere primitive in the webview of a tool that already runs subprocesses against the user's interpreters.
